declarations.documentation:
One model step over the conversation + tool schemas — THE provider seam. A provider module serves
this request for the extent of a continuation (`use <some provider>.provider(...)`), so the loop stays
provider-agnostic and providers stay loop-agnostic. The reply is an OUTCOME sum, never a throw: on
success `inferred(result)` carries the step's decision AND its token accounting (`types.step_result`,
so any loop over this seam can meter its context for free); on failure `inference_failed(error)`
carries the `step_error` the provider gave up on (its retries exhausted, or a fatal status). Handing the
failure back as a VALUE — rather than throwing from the provider's DEEP handler — is what lets each loop
decide at its own PERFORM site whether to absorb the failure (the region loop abandons just that turn and
lives on) or re-raise it into its own caller (the one-shot loops): a deep handler can only throw OUT of
its own context, never INTO the loop's, so the resume value is the only channel that reaches the loop.
declarations.name: infer_step

anyOf.description: call_turn: A conversation turn recording the model's tool-call batch — replayed so the next step shows the model what it already asked for.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
tool_call: One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key and the
model-facing call/response record), @ref@ is the call's opaque correlation handle, @args@ is the model's
argument object as a parsed value (replayed verbatim into the call turn, and dispatched straight
through `reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary unconditionally turns any `$katari_ref` the
model replayed into the `file` it denotes).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: result_turn: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:

function response, and that call's tool @name@ so the record stays readable (and so a wire that keys

screenshot an MCP tool returned, an edited image): @text@ already shows their `$katari_ref` handles
(the result's wire form), and a provider that can additionally inline their content does so while the
result is fresh.

anyOf.description:

attached to it (a chat attachment, a generated image). Files ride as blob handles; each provider decides

OPTIONAL opaque end-user tag of a user turn (e.g. a hashed chat-user id) — never shown to the model;

Schemas of its input, output and requests — each schema a plain document value, ready to embed in an AI

input.description: The input record's JSON Schema, as a document value.

name.description: The qualified name; empty for a local closure.

anyOf.description:
inference_failed: One model step's OUTCOME failure: the provider gave up — a transient error past its retry budget, or a
fatal status / malformed body. Carried back as a VALUE so a loop handles it at its perform site, rather than
the provider throwing out of its own deep handler and unwinding the whole loop with it.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]) -> T1 with infer_object | throw[provider_error | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error | validation_error]
declarations.documentation:
Infer a single reply as a typed value — structured output with the type as the contract:
`reflection.schema_of[T]` reifies T's schema, the ambient provider decodes against it natively
(a response schema, a response format, a forced tool — whichever its API offers), and the decoded object
validates as T (`json.validate` — a nonconforming reply throws `json.validation_error`). Instantiate
T explicitly; it appears only in the result, so it is never inferable. An object type
(`type shape = { ... }`) makes the friendliest model-facing schema — a data type asks the model to
produce its `$katari_constructor` wrapper too.
declarations.name: infer_structured

declarations.checkedType: agent(error: provider_error | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error) -> boolean
declarations.documentation:
Whether a step error is TRANSIENT — worth a backoff and a retry — as opposed to fatal. A transport
failure (`http.fetch_error`: DNS, a refused connection, a timeout, a mid-flight restart) is always
transient; an `http.api_error` is transient for 408 (request timeout), 429 (rate limit) and any 5xx
(server-side), and fatal for every other status (400/404 … — a retry will not fix them); an
`http.auth_error` is ALWAYS fatal, which is the whole reason that arm exists: 401 and 403 say the
CREDENTIAL is what failed, and re-sending the same credential is a retry ladder spent on a certainty
(the recovery is a fresh resolution of it, which is an app-level `replay` decision, not a backoff).
A `json.parse_error` is fatal (a malformed body will not parse on a retry). A `provider_error` answers
with the verdict its PRODUCER wrote into it: this function cannot classify a failure it has never
seen, and guessing on the producer's behalf is how a deterministic failure earns a retry ladder.
declarations.name: is_transient

The backoff delay in milliseconds before retry @attempt@ (0-based): @base_milliseconds@ doubled per
attempt (base, 2×base, 4×base, …) and capped at one minute, so a long outage does not sleep unboundedly
between the final tries.
declarations.name: backoff_milliseconds
declarations.signature: agent backoff_milliseconds(attempt: integer, base_milliseconds: number) -> number

in — a non-2xx CLASSIFIED into the shared vocabulary (`http.classify_status`) instead of surfacing as

declarations.checkedType: agent(attempt: agent(value: null) -> (attempt_err | attempt_ok[T4]) with throw[missing_secret | server_error] | io, attempts: integer, base_milliseconds: number) -> (inference_failed | inferred[T4]) with throw[missing_secret | server_error] | io
declarations.documentation:
ONE bounded retry loop over one @attempt@ agent — the control flow all providers share, so an
off-by-one is fixed once instead of six times. Run @attempt@ up to @attempts@ times: a verdict of
`attempt_ok` answers `inferred(result)` immediately; an `attempt_err` is classified by `is_transient`
and, while there is budget left, slept off for `backoff_milliseconds(attempt, base_milliseconds)` and
tried again. A FATAL error, or a transient one past the budget, answers `inference_failed(error)` — a
VALUE, never a throw, because that is what the seam promises its caller (see `infer_step`).

The DECISIONS stay exactly where they were: `is_transient` says what is worth repeating and
`backoff_milliseconds` says how long to wait, and a provider that disagrees with either overrides
nothing here — it hands back a `provider_error` carrying its own `transient` verdict. What this owns is
only the loop. @attempts@ below 1 is a configuration defect, and it answers as one: a
`provider_error` from this middleware naming the knob, marked NOT transient, because no amount of
waiting turns a zero budget into a call.
declarations.name: with_retries

parameters.label: base_milliseconds

@content_type@ in the one form both a dispatch and a wire field can use: the media type alone,
lowercased, with any parameter dropped ("Text/Plain; charset=utf-8" becomes "text/plain"), and a
confirmed alias resolved to the registered type (`canonical_content_type`). RFC 2045 makes a media type
case-insensitive and lets a sender append parameters, and an HTTP download records exactly those forms — so
the raw string is the wrong thing to compare (`application/pdf; version=1.7` would miss the PDF arm and read
as unreadable) and the wrong thing to ship (a provider's `media_type` field takes the bare type).

declarations.documentation:
An ALIAS resolved to the registered media type for the same format — the second half of normalization,
after case and parameters. A sender that derived its label from a file extension writes `image/jpg` for the
JPEG it is sending, and the accepted-type lists (the providers' and IANA's alike) name only `image/jpeg`:
without this the file takes the unreadable note although the API would have read it happily. Resolving the
alias is strictly better than either alternative — it inlines, and nothing off-list is ever sent.
Only labels CONFIRMED to name the identical format belong here. An unconfirmed guess turns a recoverable
note into a 400, which is the trade this whole dispatch exists to avoid; deliberately absent, for that
reason, are `image/pjpeg` (an IE-era label MDN's image-types guide does not equate to `image/jpeg`),
`audio/mpeg` (RFC 3003 covers MPEG-1/2 layers I–III, so it is not necessarily the MP3 that Gemini's
`audio/mp3` names) and `application/x-pdf` (no registry or vendor document equates it).

declarations.documentation:
A textual file as text the model reads: a header naming the handle and the content type, then the
decoded content, cut at @max_characters@ code points with an explicit marker when it overflows. The
marker is not decoration — a model that cannot tell it is holding a FRAGMENT answers confidently from
the fragment. The 24000-code-point default is ~6k tokens: half again the `web` package's page budget,
because an attachment cannot be re-read at another offset the way a page can be re-fetched, and still
small enough that several attachments fit one turn.

declarations.documentation:
A file's bytes decoded as UTF-8 text — the read behind `file_text_note`. The whole content transits the
value plane because the runtime has no partial-read primitive; it is a PRIM read, recomputed on replay
rather than recorded, so nothing durable grows by the file's size. A gone handle reads as "", the same
recovery as `file_content_type` (classification already routes a gone handle to `opaque_file`, so this is

declarations.documentation:
Tool: read a file that is in this conversation — an image, a PDF, or a text document. Pass the file's
handle object; a bare {"$katari_ref": "<id>"} suffices (copy the id from the conversation).
A text document (`text/*`, JSON, XML, CSV) comes back AS TEXT in this tool's result, cut at a cap with an
explicit truncation marker when it is long. An image, a PDF, audio or video comes back as the file itself,
which the model connection places in your context if its API accepts that type — so if the content does
not appear, say you cannot see it rather than guessing. A content type nothing can read (an archive, an
office document, an unrecorded type) comes back as a note saying exactly that, and reporting it is then
the correct answer.

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E5 lacks race_settled}], unbounded_tool_names?: array[string]) -> string with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool | provider_error | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | {...E5 lacks throw | race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Run the tool-using model loop, generic over the tools' shared effect @E@: derive each tool's schema
with `reflection.get_metadata`, then up to @max_steps@ times perform `infer_step` against the ambient
provider; on a batch of tool calls, dispatch them all CONCURRENTLY with `parallel for` (each resolves
its tool by name and invokes it by value via `reflection.call_agent`, validating the model's args
against the tool's schema), then feed every result back as a new turn; on a final answer, return it.
declarations.name: infer_with_tools

parameters.documentation: The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` (the default) for no deadline — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: Tool names exempt from the deadline race (human-latency tools) — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: unbounded_tool_names

declarations.signature: agent infer_with_tools[effect E](history: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null, unbounded_tool_names: array[string] ?= []) -> string

declarations.documentation:
WHO a step is on behalf of: the @author@ of the NEWEST user turn in @history@ — taken AS-IS, null
included, with no further scanning back. The newest user turn is the turn that triggered the current
model turn, so a system-triggered turn (a monitor tick, whose injection carries `author = null`)
shields the earlier human turns instead of misattributing the step to whoever spoke last; the
loop-synthesized user turns (the budget close, the empty-final renudge) are also null and likewise
read as unattributed. A provider whose API has an end-user metadata field (`metadata.user_id`,
`safety_identifier`, whatever it is called there) lifts a non-null result into it; one that has no
such field ignores it.
declarations.name: attribution

declarations.documentation:
The one-shot renudge a loop plays when the model's final step came back EMPTY: an empty string is
a lost answer in an interactive exchange (a thinking model can finish a heavy turn with only thought
parts and no text), so the loop asks ONCE for a plain-text answer before accepting the silence. The
wording also names the legitimate way out — a watcher protocol with truly nothing to report answers
empty again, and the second empty is accepted as-is.
declarations.name: empty_reply_nudge

declarations.checkedType: agent(budget_milliseconds: null | number, call: tool_call, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E6 lacks race_settled}], unbounded_tool_names?: array[string]) -> dispatched with {...E6 lacks throw | race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Find the tool whose metadata name is the model's pick and invoke it by value via
`reflection.call_agent` (the model's args ride as a plain value, and the delegation boundary
validates them against the tool's schema — the compiled signature of a Katari agent, or the
server-declared schema of an MCP tool — while the boundary's unconditional wire→value conversion turns
any replayed `$katari_ref` into the `file` it denotes). Every way a call can go wrong is fed back to the
model as an error result it reads and corrects on its next step: a hallucinated name (nothing matches), a
tool that panics, a tool's own typed `throw`, malformed args (a `reflection.call_error` from the
boundary), and a call that outruns @budget_milliseconds@ (raced via `time.with_deadline`, the late
call cancelled) alike — none of them reaches the app root. A thrown payload carrying a string `message`
field is shown to the model AS THAT LINE — a tool that wrote a sentence for a reader wrote it for this
reader — and anything else falls back to the payload's JSON. Each of those also yields a `tool_event`, so
what the model was told is not the ONLY record of it. The result's `file` values are collected off the
result tree so the provider can show them to the model (their `$katari_ref` handles are already visible in
the result text).
declarations.name: dispatch_one

parameters.documentation: The per-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` for no deadline.
parameters.label: budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: Metadata names exempt from the deadline race — human-latency tools; see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: unbounded_tool_names

declarations.signature: agent dispatch_one[effect E](tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], call: types.tool_call, budget_milliseconds: number | null, unbounded_tool_names: array[string] ?= []) -> dispatched

declarations.documentation:
Collect every `file` value out of a tool result's value tree: `reflection.call_agent` returns the
tool's result as a plain value, so a `file` the tool produced (a generated image, an MCP tool's
screenshot) is an actual `file` leaf — found wherever it sits (a bare return, the MCP bridge's
{ text, files } record, or nested structure).
declarations.name: collect_result_files
declarations.signature: agent collect_result_files(node: unknown) -> array[file] with pure

@policy.keep_recent@ elements, extended to a clean turn boundary) is summarized by one tool-less
model step under @policy.prompt@, and the summary replaces it as a single opening turn. A history
that is all tail comes back unchanged. Exported on its own so a hand-rolled loop can compact too —
`serve_session` is this plus the metering that decides when.

echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its

anyOf.description:
inference_failed: One model step's OUTCOME failure: the provider gave up — a transient error past its retry budget, or a
fatal status / malformed body. Carried back as a VALUE so a loop handles it at its perform site, rather than
the provider throwing out of its own deep handler and unwinding the whole loop with it.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

A turn the provider FAILED mid-way: the conversation as far as it got (completed call / result
exchanges included), the step error, and the tool calls that DID run before it (a failure at step
five does not un-run steps one to four). `take_turn` hands failure back as a VALUE so a long-lived
caller — an app-owned event loop — can ABSORB it as one match arm (annotate the conversation, notify
a channel, await the next event) instead of unwinding; a one-shot caller re-raises it
(`infer_with_tools`, `serve_session`).

provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

budget exhaustion and the empty-final renudge — both must commit to an answer without tools, and
both hand a provider failure back as a value. @events@ are the turn's tool calls so far, carried
through the close so a caller sees the whole turn's tool traffic whichever way it ended.

declarations.checkedType: agent(conversation: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], max_steps: integer, nudge_empty_reply?: boolean, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E7 lacks race_settled}], unbounded_tool_names?: array[string]) -> (failed_turn | session_turn) with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool] | {...E7 lacks throw | race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
THE turn loop — advance @conversation@ by one model turn and hand back a VALUE either way: up to
@max_steps@ steps against the ambient provider, tool batches dispatched in parallel, the model's
reply appended as a model turn, and the LAST step's `input + output` carried out as the context
measurement (each step's input covers the whole context, so only the freshest figure is the
occupancy — steps do not add). Budget spent, one forced tool-less close commits to an answer; an
EMPTY final is renudged once for a plain-text answer (an empty here is a lost answer, not a signal —
a caller whose protocol gives the empty reply meaning still receives the second empty as-is). A
provider failure at any step returns `failed_turn` rather than unwinding, so an app-owned event loop
absorbs it as one match arm. This is the ai package's ONE loop: sessions (`serve_session`) and
resident agents (an app-owned `observation` handler over a `region` nursery) are compositions over
it. The knobs are policy the caller owns: @tool_budget_milliseconds@ deadlines every tool call
(null = no deadline), @unbounded_tool_names@ exempts the named human-latency tools from that
deadline, and @nudge_empty_reply@ = false accepts an empty final as-is — for a caller
whose protocol gives the empty reply meaning (a watcher that stays quiet), so a quiet turn does not
pay the renudge's extra step.
declarations.name: take_turn

parameters.documentation:
The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds — every call races it via `time.with_deadline`, and a timeout
comes back to the model as an error result. `null` (the default) sets no deadline.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation:
The metadata names of tools EXEMPT from the deadline race — the human-latency tools: an
approval-gated adapter that blocks on an operator's click, an MCP call that may park on an OAuth
authorization. The doctrine: a deadline bounds MACHINE latency, and a pending ask or park is visible
in the admin surface while it waits, so such a call may be left unbounded rather than cancelled
mid-ask. Defaults to none — every tool stays under the budget.
parameters.label: unbounded_tool_names

parameters.documentation:
Whether an empty final reply is renudged once for a plain-text answer (the interactive default).
Pass `false` when the empty reply is a meaningful signal in your protocol.
parameters.label: nudge_empty_reply

declarations.signature: agent take_turn[effect E](conversation: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with {...E, prelude.throw[unknown]}], max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null ?= null, unbounded_tool_names: array[string] ?= [], nudge_empty_reply: boolean ?= true) -> turn_result

declarations.checkedType: agent(context: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], continuation: agent(value: null) -> T8 with session_message | {...E9 lacks race_settled}, max_steps: integer, policy?: compaction, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with throw[unknown] | {...E9 lacks race_settled}], unbounded_tool_names?: array[string]) -> T8 with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool | provider_error | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error] | {...E9 lacks race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Serve a chat session for the extent of @continuation@ — the hand-rolled serve skeleton as one
provider, with token metering and automatic compaction. The handler's var carries the conversation
across messages (durable by construction: it survives a runtime restart like any run state); each
`session_message` runs one tool loop and answers with the reply. After each turn the freshest
measured occupancy is classified against @threshold_tokens@: over it, the conversation compacts
(`compact`) under @compact_prompt@, keeping the last @keep_recent@ elements verbatim. The ambient
provider (the `use <some provider>.provider(...)` line) and any @E@ handlers are installed by the caller, exactly as
for `infer_with_tools`; the continuation bridges its transport into `session_message` and typically
never returns (a `watch_messages` loop).

IT HAS NO BACKLOG, deliberately and unlike a DESK. A provider failure RE-RAISES at the perform site
(this is one-shot per message), and at that moment the arriving message is in neither the conversation
nor any held queue — it exists only as the argument of the `session_message` call that is unwinding, so
a bridge that does not catch and re-deliver LOSES it. That is the right trade for a chat session, where
the sender is present and can say it again; it is the wrong one for a resident nobody is watching, which
is what `advance_desk` (a bounded backlog, a dropped marker, the shed) exists for. Reach for the desk the
moment the arrivals stop having a human behind them.
declarations.name: serve_session

parameters.documentation:
The conversation the model starts from (PRIOR TURNS only — standing instructions belong in the
provider's `system` parameter, which every provider takes and compaction never touches; anything put
here is history, and the first compaction folds it into the summary).

parameters.label: tools

parameters.documentation: The per-message step budget.
parameters.label: max_steps

parameters.label: policy

parameters.documentation: The per-tool-call budget in milliseconds, or `null` (the default) for no deadline — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: tool_budget_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: Tool names exempt from the deadline race (human-latency tools) — see `take_turn`.
parameters.label: unbounded_tool_names

parameters.documentation: The session body: bridges a transport into `session_message`.

declarations.documentation:
THE event→model channel: a background fiber (an always-on source such as a chat watcher, or a
started watch) pushes @content@ (plus any @files@) from @source@ into the model's context.
FIRE-AND-FORGET (`-> null`): a fiber only reports — the app's serving handler injects the report as
a user turn, advances the conversation (`take_turn`), and routes the reply wherever it belongs.
@files@ ride the injection turn's `files` slot — the same text + files split as `types.turn` — so
the provider's existing inline policy shows the model any attached image. @author@ rides the
injection turn's `author`, so the triggered turn's requests carry the right abuse-attribution
metadata (`ai.attribution`).

declarations.checkedType: agent(prompt: agent(value: null) -> string with E10, schedule: cron | interval, source: string) -> never with observation | E10 | io
declarations.documentation:
A watch body reduced to its essence: on every occurrence of @schedule@, inject the freshly
computed @prompt@ into the model's context as an observation from @source@ — the scheduled
self-prompt every periodic watcher (check a repo, track a topic, look at a calendar) hand-rolled as
its own `time.watch` adapter. @prompt@ is an agent so each tick recomputes it (an env-configured
target re-reads, a date renders current); its effects @E@ flow to the app's handlers. Never returns:
fork it into the app's nursery and cancel its fiber to stop.
declarations.name: watch_prompt

parameters.documentation: Which watcher is reporting; labels the injection turn (e.g. "repo-issues").
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: Computes the report to inject, fresh at every occurrence.
parameters.label: prompt

parameters.documentation: When occurrences fire: `time.interval(...)` or `time.cron(...)`.
parameters.label: schedule

declarations.documentation:
ONE thing that arrived for a desk — the same text + files + author split as `types.turn`, plus the
PROVENANCE pair every multi-agent program ended up needing: @source@, which labels the injected turn so
the model can tell a chat message from a cron tick from another agent's mail, and @hop@, how many
agent-to-agent relays it has already made.
declarations.name: arrival

parameters.documentation: Who is reporting (e.g. "discord:<channel>", "cron:morning"); labels the injected turn.
parameters.label: source

parameters.documentation: The message body.
parameters.label: content

parameters.documentation:
How many agent-to-agent hops this message has already made: 0 for anything that is not mail between
agents (a chat message, a cron tick, a watch report, a session's own startup line), 1 for a first-hop
send, 2 for the reply to one. It is a fact about the MESSAGE, so it is carried and not guessed — a
program that damps replies ("a reply that asks nothing needs no answer") cannot state that rule at all
while every sender stamps the same constant.

declarations.documentation:
THE PROVENANCE OF THE ARRIVAL THIS DESK IS SERVING RIGHT NOW: @origin@ is the arrival's `source`
verbatim and @hop@ is its `hop`. Served by `advance_desk` for the extent of ONE dispatch — the desk is
the only frame holding the arrival, and a desk's tool set is assembled once for the whole session, so a
tool cannot close over the message it is answering.

TOOLS READ THIS INSTEAD OF PARSING THE LABEL. The injected turn opens with prose ("Message from
<source>:"), and a tool that wanted the sender or the hop used to recover it by pattern-matching that
sentence — which makes a display string load-bearing and puts the hop rule at the mercy of a reworded
line. Here both halves are the values the caller put in the `arrival`. The label stays what it is, a
label for the model to read.

A program with no desk serving it (a hand-rolled `take_turn`) simply has no handler for this, and a tool
that performs it says so in its own effect row — so the capability is visible in the type rather than
assumed.
declarations.name: inbound_provenance

ordinary chat shape, where the conversation owes one answer per message.

times or five, to whichever channel a tool allows. The text is discarded, and the discard is ANNOUNCED

believing it answered, not a model choosing silence.

declarations.signature: data desk_policy(max_steps: integer, tool_budget_milliseconds: number | null, unbounded_tool_names: array[string], compaction_policy: compaction, backlog_retention: integer, reply: reply_policy)

declarations.documentation:
The default desk policy: 16 steps per arrival, a 60-second deadline on every tool call, no
exemptions, the default compaction, 24 held arrivals, and the reply delivered. The retention figure is
the bound on what an outage costs the returning conversation — a night of messages against a dead
provider comes back as the newest two dozen plus one line saying how many were dropped.
declarations.name: default_desk_policy

passes it to every desk (or a different one per desk; it is data).

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

What `advance_desk` hands back: the desk as it now stands, what happened, and the turn's tool calls.
The state and the outcome move TOGETHER — a filed arrival advances the backlog and not the
conversation, an answered one advances the conversation and clears the backlog — so they are one value
and the app writes its var from `state` without re-deciding anything.

items.description:
tool_call: One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key and the
model-facing call/response record), @ref@ is the call's opaque correlation handle, @args@ is the model's
argument object as a parsed value (replayed verbatim into the call turn, and dispatched straight
through `reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary unconditionally turns any `$katari_ref` the
model replayed into the `file` it denotes).

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

conversation, an answered one advances the conversation and clears the backlog — so they are one value
and the app writes its var from `state` without re-deciding anything.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
answered: What one arrival did to a desk: the model ANSWERED. @reply@ is the turn's final text — blank when the
model chose silence, and already delivered when the policy says to deliver.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

reply.description: The turn's final text; blank means the model had nothing to say.

anyOf.description:
filed: What one arrival did to a desk: the model was NOT CALLED AT ALL — a breaker is open — so the arrival
went into the backlog and no model call was spent. @held@ and @dropped@ are the backlog as it now
stands.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

dropped.description: How many the bound has discarded in total.

held.description: How many arrivals the desk is now holding.

anyOf.description:
step_failed: What one arrival did to a desk: the model was called and the step FAILED. The arrival is in the
backlog (so nothing is lost), the stored conversation is untouched (so the outage costs it nothing),
and the attachments of a REFUSED call have been shed. The error rides out for the app to report on;
the desk has already survived it.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

declarations.checkedType: agent(kind: needs_operator | waits_out, messages: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]) -> array[call_turn | result_turn | turn]
declarations.documentation:
THE shed decision, made once from the outage classification: a REFUSED call's messages lose their
attachments, a passing failure's messages keep every one. `needs_operator` is exactly the family that
repeats deterministically — the same request meets the same refusal however long anyone waits — and an
attachment is the one part of the request whose acceptability an app cannot test before sending. A
`waits_out` failure sheds nothing: a rate limit is not the image's fault. The imprecision inside the
refused family is accepted with open eyes (a revoked key sheds files that were innocent), because
telling the-file-did-it from the-key-did-it would mean parsing provider error prose, and a shed
attachment is a noted, re-askable loss while a poisoned conversation is a desk nothing revives.
declarations.name: shed_refused

parameters.documentation: What the failure said about who can end it.
parameters.label: kind

parameters.documentation: The messages that rode the failed call.
parameters.label: messages

anyOf.description:
needs_operator: What a failed step says about who can end the outage: a PERSON must act. A 400 (a spent credit
balance, a model name the provider no longer serves), a 401 or a 403 (a wrong, revoked or
under-privileged key), a 404 (an unknown model) do not heal with time, so @remedy@ carries the one
clause that turns an evening of silence into a five-minute fix.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

remedy.description: What to check, in one clause.

anyOf.description:
waits_out: What a failed step says about who can end the outage: NOBODY — it is the kind that passes. A rate
limit, a 5xx, a dropped connection, a reply the provider could not make sense of. The provider has
already spent its retry budget on it, so the only jobs left are to stop hammering while it lasts and to
say nothing an operator cannot act on.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

kind.description: What the failure said about who can end it.

messages.description: The messages that rode the failed call.

model-facing call/response record), @ref@ is the call's opaque correlation handle, @args@ is the model's
argument object as a parsed value (replayed verbatim into the call turn, and dispatched straight
through `reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary unconditionally turns any `$katari_ref` the
model replayed into the `file` it denotes).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: result_turn: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

function response, and that call's tool @name@ so the record stays readable (and so a wire that keys

screenshot an MCP tool returned, an edited image): @text@ already shows their `$katari_ref` handles
(the result's wire form), and a provider that can additionally inline their content does so while the
result is fresh.

declarations.documentation:
File one arrival into a desk's backlog, bounded: keep the newest @retention@ and count what fell off
the front. Written as arithmetic on the window rather than as a branch, so there is no is-it-full-yet
case to get wrong — an unfilled backlog slices from 0 and drops nothing.

declarations.signature: agent hold_arrival(held: backlog, message: types.message, retention: integer) -> backlog

declarations.documentation:
The ONE line that stands in for what a backlog's bound discarded, or no line at all when it discarded
nothing. It is DERIVED from the count on every attempt rather than appended to the stored conversation,
so an outage that spans ten failed probes still produces one line and not ten; the turn that finally
ANSWERS bakes that single line in and clears the count with the backlog it stood for.
declarations.name: dropped_marker

parameters.documentation: How many arrivals the bound discarded.
parameters.label: dropped

The conversation ONE turn actually runs on: the desk's stored conversation, plus the derived
dropped-marker and whatever the backlog is holding. This is where a held backlog rejoins the
conversation, and it happens at the ATTEMPT, not at the filing, which is what keeps a desk that cannot
be served frozen.

declarations.checkedType: agent(arrival: arrival, deliver_to: agent(reply: string) -> null with {...E11 lacks race_settled}, persona: agent(value: null) -> string with infer_step | {...E11 lacks race_settled}, policy?: desk_policy, state: desk, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with inbound_provenance | throw[unknown] | {...E11 lacks race_settled}]) -> desk_turn with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool] | {...E11 lacks inbound_provenance | race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
ADVANCE ONE DESK by one arrival — the whole of a resident conversation's per-message behaviour, as a
function from a desk and an arrival to the next desk. The arrival injects as a user turn onto the
desk's conversation PLUS whatever the backlog holds; one `take_turn` runs under `with_context(inject =
persona)`, so a per-turn persona re-derives at every model step and is never persisted; a blank final
is not renudged (silence is a legitimate answer for a resident). Then, by outcome:

— ANSWERED: the reply is delivered or discarded-and-announced per @policy.reply@, the backlog is
  cleared (it rejoined the conversation on this turn), and an over-budget conversation compacts.
— REFUSED BY A BREAKER (`with_breaker` is installed and open): no model call was spent — the arrival
  is filed into the bounded backlog and the stored conversation is untouched.
— FAILED: the same filing, plus the SHED — a call the provider refused loses the attachments it
  carried, across the whole backlog, because everything in it rode that call and re-rides every later
  one. The stored conversation stays frozen here too: a failed turn's partial tool work is discarded
  rather than preserved, because preserving it grows an outage's cost with the outage's length and
  re-sends whatever the provider refused. The arrival is not lost — it is in the backlog, and the turn
  that recovers reads it.

Tools and @persona@ are ordinary parameters, so a program with several desks passes a different set
and a different voice per desk without holding either in the desk's state.

FOR THE EXTENT OF THE DISPATCH IT SERVES `inbound_provenance`, answering with this arrival's `source`
and `hop`. A desk's tool set is assembled once for the session, so a tool cannot close over the message
it is answering — and the desk is the one frame that holds it. A tool that relays mail therefore stamps
the NEXT hop from what actually arrived, and reads the sender as a value instead of parsing it back out
of the injected turn's prose.
declarations.name: advance_desk

declarations.checkedType: agent(continuation: agent(value: null) -> T12 with observation | {...E13 lacks race_settled}, deliver_to: agent(reply: string) -> null with {...E13 lacks race_settled}, max_steps: integer, policy?: compaction, tool_budget_milliseconds?: number, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with inbound_provenance | throw[unknown] | {...E13 lacks race_settled}], unbounded_tool_names?: array[string]) -> T12 with infer_step | throw[duplicate_tool] | {...E13 lacks race_settled} | io
declarations.documentation:
Serve a SINGLE resident conversation's observations for the extent of @continuation@ — the simple
form: one desk behind one handler var, each `observation` advancing it (`advance_desk`) and the reply
leaving through @deliver_to@. THE RESIDENT PROTOCOL IS BUILT IN: an empty (blank) reply means 'nothing
to say' — it is not delivered and not renudged, so a quiet watcher tick costs exactly one model step.
Every desk behaviour comes with it (a bounded backlog, the dropped marker, the shed).

FOR MORE THAN ONE CONVERSATION, GO TO THE DESK API. This serves exactly one: a program that grows a
second addressee — a public-facing character beside a private one, a table of workers — cannot express
it here, because there is one var and one tool set. `advance_desk` is this same behaviour with the
routing left to you, and `with_breaker` is the outage policy for ALL of your desks at once.

A provider failure is ABSORBED (a resident must outlive a failed step) and NOTIFIED ONCE, on the
transition: the first failure after a run of good turns delivers one line, the failures after it
deliver nothing, and the turn that recovers delivers one line back. Per-turn notification is what
turned a delivery backlog plus a standing outage into sixteen identical messages in seconds; the
transition test is the fix, and installing `with_breaker` additionally stops the doomed calls.
declarations.name: serve_observations

serves it, always with `hop = 0` (an observation is a report, never a relay).

declarations.documentation:
One key's stored desk, tagged with the launch @generation@ its conversation belongs to — the table's
cell. The table discards a cell whose generation an arrival supersedes (the name was reused), so a
reused key never inherits the previous incarnation's conversation. Internal to the table's machinery; an
app reaches a desk through `advance_in_table`, never this.

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

declarations.documentation:
A TABLE of keyed resident desks: for each key, the desk and the generation it belongs to, in one
value. OPAQUE by contract — a program builds it with `new_desk_table`, advances a key through
`advance_in_table`, drops one with `forget_desk`, reads a key's generation with `desk_generation`, and
reaches into @cells@ for nothing else. Durable by construction wherever the app keeps it (a handler var
survives a runtime restart like any run state); a program holds one per collection of dynamically keyed
conversations.
declarations.name: desk_table

parameters.documentation: The keyed cells; OPAQUE — use the table's own functions, not this field.
parameters.label: cells

declarations.documentation:
A fresh, empty desk table — no keys, no desks. A program installs one per collection of dynamically
keyed conversations (a worker table); its fixed desks stay their own vars.
declarations.name: new_desk_table

output.description:
desk_table: A TABLE of keyed resident desks: for each key, the desk and the generation it belongs to, in one
value. OPAQUE by contract — a program builds it with `new_desk_table`, advances a key through
`advance_in_table`, drops one with `forget_desk`, reads a key's generation with `desk_generation`, and
reaches into @cells@ for nothing else. Durable by construction wherever the app keeps it (a handler var
survives a runtime restart like any run state); a program holds one per collection of dynamically keyed
conversations.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

additionalProperties.description:
keyed_desk: One key's stored desk, tagged with the launch @generation@ its conversation belongs to — the table's
cell. The table discards a cell whose generation an arrival supersedes (the name was reused), so a
reused key never inherits the previous incarnation's conversation. Internal to the table's machinery; an
app reaches a desk through `advance_in_table`, never this.

declarations.documentation:
What `advance_in_table` did: the arrival was SERVED — a desk took the turn (the key's own, or a fresh
one when the key was new or its generation superseded). @turn@ is the whole `advance_desk` result — the
desk's per-arrival outcome (`answered` / `filed` / `step_failed`), its new state (already written back
into the returned table), and its tool events — so a program that cares about the desk-level outcome
reads it here, and one that does not just writes the table back.
declarations.name: advanced

parameters.documentation: The desk's turn — `advance_desk`'s full result.

anyOf.description:
answered: What one arrival did to a desk: the model ANSWERED. @reply@ is the turn's final text — blank when the
model chose silence, and already delivered when the policy says to deliver.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

reply.description: The turn's final text; blank means the model had nothing to say.

anyOf.description:
filed: What one arrival did to a desk: the model was NOT CALLED AT ALL — a breaker is open — so the arrival
went into the backlog and no model call was spent. @held@ and @dropped@ are the backlog as it now
stands.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

dropped.description: How many the bound has discarded in total.

held.description: How many arrivals the desk is now holding.

anyOf.description:
step_failed: What one arrival did to a desk: the model was called and the step FAILED. The arrival is in the
backlog (so nothing is lost), the stored conversation is untouched (so the outage costs it nothing),
and the attachments of a REFUSED call have been shed. The error rides out for the app to report on;
the desk has already survived it.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

declarations.documentation:
What `advance_in_table` did: NOTHING — the arrival's generation was OLDER than the one the table holds
for its key, so it is a straggler from a superseded incarnation of a reused name. It is dropped, the
table is left exactly as it was, and no model call is spent. @arrival_generation@ is what the arrival
carried and @current_generation@ is what the table holds, so a program can log precisely which
incarnation's message it discarded.

declarations.documentation:
What `advance_in_table` hands back: the table as it now stands, what happened, and the turn's tool
calls. The table and the outcome move TOGETHER, exactly as `desk_turn` pairs a desk with its outcome — a
served arrival advanced some key's desk and @table@ has it written back, a stale one changed nothing and
@table@ is the one that went in — so the app writes its var from @table@ without re-deciding anything,
and reads @tool_events@ (empty on `stale`, nothing having run) the same way whichever way the turn
went.
declarations.name: table_turn

stale: What `advance_in_table` did: NOTHING — the arrival's generation was OLDER than the one the table holds

carried and @current_generation@ is what the table holds, so a program can log precisely which
incarnation's message it discarded.
