output.description:
table_turn: What `advance_in_table` hands back: the table as it now stands, what happened, and the turn's tool
calls. The table and the outcome move TOGETHER, exactly as `desk_turn` pairs a desk with its outcome — a
served arrival advanced some key's desk and @table@ has it written back, a stale one changed nothing and
@table@ is the one that went in — so the app writes its var from @table@ without re-deciding anything,
and reads @tool_events@ (empty on `stale`, nothing having run) the same way whichever way the turn
went.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
advanced: What `advance_in_table` did: the arrival was SERVED — a desk took the turn (the key's own, or a fresh
one when the key was new or its generation superseded). @turn@ is the whole `advance_desk` result — the
desk's per-arrival outcome (`answered` / `filed` / `step_failed`), its new state (already written back
into the returned table), and its tool events — so a program that cares about the desk-level outcome
reads it here, and one that does not just writes the table back.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.
The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
answered: What one arrival did to a desk: the model ANSWERED. @reply@ is the turn's final text — blank when the
model chose silence, and already delivered when the policy says to deliver.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

reply.description: The turn's final text; blank means the model had nothing to say.

anyOf.description:
filed: What one arrival did to a desk: the model was NOT CALLED AT ALL — a breaker is open — so the arrival
went into the backlog and no model call was spent. @held@ and @dropped@ are the backlog as it now
stands.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

dropped.description: How many the bound has discarded in total.

held.description: How many arrivals the desk is now holding.

anyOf.description:
step_failed: What one arrival did to a desk: the model was called and the step FAILED. The arrival is in the
backlog (so nothing is lost), the stored conversation is untouched (so the outage costs it nothing),
and the attachments of a REFUSED call have been shed. The error rides out for the app to report on;
the desk has already survived it.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

error.description: The step error the provider surfaced.

state.description: The desk after this arrival — write it back.

declarations.documentation:
ADVANCE ONE KEY'S DESK in a table by one arrival — the keyed sibling of `advance_desk`, with the
reused-name generation rule folded in. Look @key@ up in @table@, then decide by how @generation@ (the
arrival's, minted by the app's roster at admit and carried here) compares with what the table holds:

— KEY ABSENT: a fresh `new_desk` takes the turn, stored under @generation@.
— GENERATION OLDER than the cell's: the arrival is a straggler from a superseded incarnation of a reused
  name — DROPPED (`stale`), the table unchanged, no model call spent.
— GENERATION EQUAL: the ordinary case — the held desk takes the turn, one more message in the same
  incarnation's conversation.
— GENERATION NEWER than the cell's: the name was reused and the held desk is the PREVIOUS incarnation's,
  so it is discarded and a fresh `new_desk` takes the turn under @generation@ — a reused name never
  inherits the dismissed one's conversation or mandate.

The turn itself is `advance_desk`'s, whole and unchanged: @tools@, @persona@, @deliver_to@ and @policy@
are its parameters, passed straight through, so a table of workers gives each key its own voice and tool
set per dispatch without holding either in the table's state. This function adds only the lookup, the
fresh-desk default and the staleness verdict; the backlog, the shed and the compaction are the desk's.
declarations.name: advance_in_table

declarations.documentation:
Run one arrival against @base@ (the desk the generation rule chose) through `advance_desk`, then write
the result back into @table@ under @key@ STAMPED with @generation@ — the served half of
`advance_in_table`, shared by its three spending arms (key absent, generation equal, generation newer).
Stamping the generation on write-back is what lets a fresh desk started for a reused name record the
incarnation it belongs to, so the next arrival compares against the right number. Internal to
`advance_in_table`.

declarations.documentation:
Drop @key@ from the table — the RETIRE move. After it the table holds no desk and no generation for
the key, so the next arrival for it (should the name be admitted again) starts a fresh desk. A program
that retires a worker by dropping it from its roster forgets its desk here in the same breath. Forgetting
a key the table never held is a no-op.

conversations.

The generation the table holds for @key@ — the incarnation its stored conversation belongs to — or
`null` when the table holds no desk for the key. A reader for observation and tests: the generation an
arrival is COMPARED against is the app's to mint and lives in its roster, and this reports what the table
last STORED, not what the roster now says. (The table offers no way to SET a generation for this reason —
the roster is the one source of truth for which incarnation a name is on.)

declarations.documentation:
WHY one supervised attempt ended, split into the part that is COMPARED and the part that is READ.
@kind@ is the reason's stable identity — a short tag the app picks for the failure's shape ("panic",
"discord-source-died", a thrown error's constructor name) — and it is the only thing the backoff
looks at. @detail@ is the line a human reads and may carry anything: an id, a timestamp, a quoted
message. Splitting them is the point: comparing whole prose, which is what this replaced, means a
message carrying an id or a timestamp NEVER equals the previous one, so a sustained outage looks like
a fresh failure every time, the backoff resets to its floor on every restart, and the notice that was
meant to go quiet shouts identically forever. The set of an app's crash kinds is the app's own, which
is why @kind@ is a string here and not a sum this package could not have written.
declarations.name: crash_reason

declarations.checkedType: agent(factor?: number, initial_delay_milliseconds?: number, max_delay_milliseconds?: number, on_restart: agent(event: first_failure | repeated_failure) -> null with E16, session: agent(value: null) -> crash_reason with E16) -> never with E16 | io
declarations.documentation:
Supervise a restartable @session@ FOREVER: run one attempt, and when it ends by RETURNING a
recoverable `crash_reason`, call @on_restart@, wait the current backoff, and start a fresh attempt. The
backoff starts at @initial_delay_milliseconds@ and grows by @factor@ each time the reason's KIND repeats
(a sustained outage), capped at @max_delay_milliseconds@; a changed kind resets it to the floor. @on_restart@ hears
a `restart_event`, so a repeat is a distinguishable value carrying its streak rather than a boolean
flag beside a string. Fatal-vs-restartable is the SESSION's decision, not this loop's: a session that
hits an unrecoverable error re-raises it, and it propagates through `supervise` UNTOUCHED to a handler
the app installed above; `supervise` only ever sees the reason a session hands back by RETURNING, and
every such return is a restart. Returns `never` — the loop ends only when a session's fatal re-raise
unwinds past it.
declarations.name: supervise

parameters.label: initial_delay_milliseconds

parameters.documentation: The factor the backoff grows by while the same kind repeats. Default 2.
parameters.label: factor

parameters.documentation: The backoff ceiling in milliseconds — the growing delay never exceeds it. Default 15 minutes.

declarations.checkedType: agent(continuation: agent(value: null) -> T17 with infer_step | E18, inject: agent(value: null) -> string with infer_step | E18) -> T17 with infer_step | E18
declarations.documentation:
Middleware over the seam: EVERY `infer_step`, insert @inject@'s freshly computed text as a user turn
JUST BEFORE the newest user turn, and re-perform outward to the ambient provider — the generalization
of the bot-side pattern that re-injects the current time and a memory index each turn. Install it
INSIDE the provider (the provider's `use` first, then `use ai.with_context(inject = ...)`), so the
re-performed step reaches the model. An EMPTY injection skips the extra turn; the injected turn is
never part of the conversation a loop persists (it is derived fresh each step, so persisting it would
double it). `infer_object` passes through un-injected — structured extraction states its own context.

WHY BEFORE THE NEWEST USER TURN AND NOT AT THE FRONT, which is where this used to put it: every model
API reuses a repeated request prefix only while it stays BYTE-IDENTICAL, and an ambient note is by
definition the part that CHANGES — a clock reading, a memory index that just gained an entry. At the
front, one changed character invalidated the whole conversation on every step, so a note carrying the
time cost a tool loop its entire prefix at every step of every turn. Here the changing bytes sit at the
END of the stable region: the newest user turn is the turn that triggered this model turn, and a turn's
tool loop only APPENDS after it, so everything from element 0 up to the injection is identical across
the steps of a turn and across turns. Recency helps too — a note the model is meant to act on now reads
better next to the message it applies to than twenty exchanges earlier.
declarations.name: with_context

parameters.documentation: Computes the note to inject this step — ambient state (the time, a memory index), fresh each step.

parameters.documentation: The program to run with the injection installed.

declarations.checkedType: agent(error: provider_error | api_error | auth_error | fetch_error | parse_error) -> (needs_operator | waits_out)
declarations.documentation:
Classify a failed step by WHO CAN END IT. The statuses a person must act on are matched as LITERALS
off the error's own `status`, so the rule reads as the list it is; everything else waits. An
`http.auth_error` is ALWAYS a person's job — 401 and 403 are the two statuses that arm exists for, and
both name a credential nobody but an operator can replace — while an `http.api_error` needs the status
read, because that arm holds a 400 (act) beside a 429 (wait). A `json.parse_error` and a
`provider_error` land in `waits_out` deliberately: they are not transient either, but there is no lever
to hand an operator for them, and sending someone to check a balance that is fine is worse than saying
nothing specific.
declarations.name: classify_outage

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

to ten minutes. THREE, because one failure is noise and two can still be one bad minute, while three in
a row means the provider itself is out. TEN MINUTES, because a dead provider is then re-tested six
times an hour for the price of one step each, which is the standing cost of being wrong about an
outage.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole

failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.

policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

declarations.documentation:
Middleware over the seam: install ONE breaker for every model call in @continuation@'s dynamic extent
— every desk, every session, every hand-rolled `take_turn` — inside the provider (the provider's `use`
first, then `use ai.with_breaker(...)`), so a refused step never reaches the provider at all.

@failure_threshold@ consecutive failed steps OPEN it; while open, `infer_step` answers
`inference_failed(breaker_refusal_error(...))` WITHOUT calling out, except for the one probe step per
interval that tests for recovery. @on_transition@ fires on the STATE CHANGE and nowhere else — once on
the way out, once on the way back — which is what makes the notice structurally un-floodable: it is
read off the state the transition just produced, so there is no count tested anywhere else and no way
for a still-closed breaker to announce. WHERE those two lines go and HOW they read is the app's data:
the sink gets the `outage_kind` (`outage_line` / `recovery_line` are the wordings this package
suggests), and an app with both an operator's channel and a public one sends the remedy to the first
and the transient wording to the second.

`infer_object` passes through un-broken: a structured extraction is a one-shot call whose caller is
right there to see it fail.

declarations.documentation:
Serve `ai.infer_step` over Anthropic for the extent of the continuation:
`use anthropic.provider(source = credentials.env(key = "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"))`.
A step's provider failure (`ai.step_error`) is handed back as an `ai.inference_failed` OUTCOME, never
thrown — but a TRANSIENT one (a 429 rate limit, a 5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with
exponential backoff (up to @retry_attempts@ attempts from @retry_base_milliseconds@); only a fatal error
or an exhausted budget surfaces, as a value the loop handles at its own perform site rather than a throw.
Prompt caching is ON and needs no argument: every step marks two `cache_control` breakpoints — one at
the end of the tools+@system@ prefix, one at the end of the conversation — so a tool loop re-reads
what it already sent at a tenth of the price. Caching is per-PROVIDER machinery (Gemini's is implicit,
OpenAI's automatic); Anthropic's is the one that must be asked for. See the prompt-caching section for
what silently undoes it.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

the Messages API accepts. An image (of an accepted media type — see `anthropic_image_blocks`) and a PDF
inline as their own block, each preceded by its handle note so the model keeps the replay affordance; a

declarations.documentation:
One tool's output, keyed back to its call — with the result's FILES inlined INSIDE the tool_result's own
content array, through the same `anthropic_file_blocks` dispatch the turn path uses. The Messages API
documents that a tool_result's content blocks "can use the `text`, `image`, `document`, or `search_result`
types", which is exactly the set that dispatch produces, so a file re-read with `ai.view_file` reaches the
model here instead of being dropped (it was dropped for as long as this provider existed).
INSIDE rather than beside the tool_result, for two documented reasons: a user message carrying tool results
may only append TEXT after them ("the tool_result blocks must come FIRST in the content array. Any text
must come AFTER all tool results"), so an image or document block beside them is not licensed; and the
API's own guidance is to keep tool content — which comes from outside the app — inside the tool_result
block rather than in a plain user text block, because that is what marks it untrusted.

declarations.documentation:
The step's token accounting off the response's `usage`. The context a step read splits across
`input_tokens` and the cache counters (`cache_read_input_tokens` / `cache_creation_input_tokens`),
so the occupancy is their sum; an absent field reads as 0. The split is a LIVE one — the provider
marks cache breakpoints (see the prompt-caching section), so a warm step reports most of its context
under `cache_read_input_tokens`, which is also how a run trace shows the cache is working.
declarations.name: anthropic_usage

output.description:
usage: One step's token accounting, as the provider's API reported it. @input_tokens@ counts the whole
context the step consumed (every provider re-reads the full history each step), so the FRESHEST
step's figure IS the session's current context occupancy — figures across steps do not add.
@output_tokens@ counts what the model generated on the step.

declarations.documentation:
Serve `ai.infer_step` over Gemini for the extent of the continuation:
`use gemini.provider(source = credentials.env(key = "GEMINI_API_KEY"))`.
A step's provider failure (malformed JSON, a rejected call, a transport failure — `ai.step_error`) is
handed back as an `ai.inference_failed` OUTCOME, never thrown — but a TRANSIENT one (a 429 rate limit, a
5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with exponential backoff (up to @retry_attempts@ attempts from
@retry_base_milliseconds@), so a passing rate limit no longer ends a long-lived loop; only a fatal error or
an exhausted budget surfaces, and it surfaces as a value the loop handles at its own perform site, not a
throw out of this deep handler.
Prompt caching is per-PROVIDER machinery and nothing here asks for it: Gemini caches a repeated prefix
IMPLICITLY, off the bytes it already receives. (Anthropic is the one that needs explicit `cache_control`
breakpoints, which `anthropic.provider` places for you.)

workhorse of the series this module is written against — the model every example, guide and integration
test in this ecosystem already names — and a DEFAULT is what runs when nobody chose, so it should be the
model a program can afford to run at every step. A program with an opinion passes it.

client.description:
connection: A Gemini connection: the model id, the API key, an optional system instruction, the optional generation
knobs, and the transient-retry budget (@retry_attempts@ / @retry_base_milliseconds@). Provider handler
state — built once per `use gemini.provider(...)`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

retry_attempts.description: How many times a transient step is attempted before its error propagates.

retry_base_milliseconds.description: The first backoff delay (ms), doubled per retry.

anyOf.description:
env: A named secret in the project's env store — `resolve` reads it with `env.get_secret` at each use,
so a rotated secret lands without a restart. Missing at resolve time throws `env.missing_secret`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

key.description: The secret entry's key in the project's env store.

anyOf.description:
oauth: A named credential in the runtime's credential store — `resolve` reads it with `oauth.token` at
each use, so a refreshed token is always the current one. An unusable credential throws
`oauth.server_error` (and may park the run on an authorization escalation, like any `oauth.token`).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

name.description: The credential's name in the runtime's credential store.

source.description: Where the API key lives (env key or oauth name); resolved at each request.

system.description: The system instruction, or `null` for none.

anyOf.description: call_turn: A conversation turn recording the model's tool-call batch — replayed so the next step shows the model what it already asked for.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
tool_call: One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key and the
model-facing call/response record), @ref@ is the call's opaque correlation handle, @args@ is the model's
argument object as a parsed value (replayed verbatim into the call turn, and dispatched straight
through `reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary unconditionally turns any `$katari_ref` the
model replayed into the `file` it denotes).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: result_turn: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
tool_result: A tool's output for the model, carrying the @ref@ of the call it answers so it round-trips as a
function response, and that call's tool @name@ so the record stays readable (and so a wire that keys
its responses by name has the name to hand). @files@ are the `file` values found in the result (a
screenshot an MCP tool returned, an edited image): @text@ already shows their `$katari_ref` handles
(the result's wire form), and a provider that can additionally inline their content does so while the
result is fresh.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description:
turn: One turn in a conversation: who spoke (`user_role` / `model_role`), what they said, and any files
attached to it (a chat attachment, a generated image). Files ride as blob handles; each provider decides
when to inline their content for the model (see the providers' inline policy). @author@ is the
OPTIONAL opaque end-user tag of a user turn (e.g. a hashed chat-user id) — never shown to the model;
a provider whose API has an abuse-attribution field lifts the newest user turn's author into it
(`ai.attribution`). `null` (the default) means the turn is not attributable to an end user: a system
framing turn, a monitor notification, a loop-synthesized turn.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.
The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
user_role: Whose turn this is: the CALLER's side of the conversation — a person's message, a system framing
turn, a background report, a turn the loop synthesized. Every provider has a token for it; none of
them is this datum.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
agent_metadata: The public metadata of one callable: its (qualified) name, its `@"..."` description, and the JSON
Schemas of its input, output and requests — each schema a plain document value, ready to embed in an AI
tool list. A local (closure) callable has an empty name.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

description.description: The `@"..."` documentation text; empty when undocumented.

input.description: The input record's JSON Schema, as a document value.

name.description: The qualified name; empty for a local closure.

output.description: The output's JSON Schema, as a document value.

requests.description: The requests' schemas: one { name, input, output } object per request the callable may perform.

anyOf.description: attempt_err: The outcome of ONE provider step attempt: the @error@ the attempt caught, for the retry loop to classify.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
attempt_ok: The outcome of ONE provider step attempt, threaded back to a provider's retry loop: the step's @result@
on success. A provider's per-attempt helper catches a `step_error` into `attempt_err` so the loop can
classify it (`is_transient`) and either back off and retry or propagate.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

result.description: step_result: What a provider returns for one model step: the decision plus its token accounting.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: step_call: One inference step's decision: invoke a batch of tools (dispatched in parallel, results fed back together).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

items.description:
tool_call: One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key and the
model-facing call/response record), @ref@ is the call's opaque correlation handle, @args@ is the model's
argument object as a parsed value (replayed verbatim into the call turn, and dispatched straight
through `reflection.call_agent`, whose delegation boundary unconditionally turns any `$katari_ref` the
model replayed into the `file` it denotes).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

ref.description:
call_ref: THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

token.description: The provider's opaque per-call token, replayed verbatim.

anyOf.description: step_final: One inference step's decision: a final reply text for the user.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

usage.description:
usage: One step's token accounting, as the provider's API reported it. @input_tokens@ counts the whole
context the step consumed (every provider re-reads the full history each step), so the FRESHEST
step's figure IS the session's current context occupancy — figures across steps do not add.
@output_tokens@ counts what the model generated on the step.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
missing_secret: No secret env entry is set under @key@. Thrown by `get_secret` — catch it to fall back in-program
(`use handler { request throw(error: env.missing_secret) -> never { ... } }`).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

key.description: The key that had no secret entry.

anyOf.description:
server_error: The OAuth token could not be resolved for a TRANSIENT reason — a network error, or the token endpoint
failing (5xx) while refreshing. Thrown by `token`. Catch it to control retry — a retried call re-resolves.
(A credential that needs a human to (re)authorize is never a throw: the run pauses on an authorization
escalation instead.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

declarations.signature: agent gemini_step_attempt(client: connection, history: array[types.message], tool_metas: array[reflection.agent_metadata]) -> ai.attempt[types.step_result] with io | prelude.throw[env.missing_secret | oauth.server_error]

declarations.checkedType: agent(client: connection, history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], schema: unknown) -> (attempt_err | attempt_ok[object_result]) with throw[missing_secret | server_error] | io
declarations.documentation: ONE Gemini structured-output attempt, the `gemini_step_attempt` twin for `infer_object`.

declarations.documentation:
Map the agnostic role sum onto the `generateContent` content role. It happens to spell the model's
side "model", which is why this is written out as a match like every other provider's rather than
passed through: the vocabulary is the sum, and a wire token that resembles it is a coincidence, not an
identity.

declarations.documentation:
THIS provider's own step failure: `generateContent` finished a step WITHOUT an answer — no function
call and no reply text — with a finish reason other than a normal stop (an output-token truncation that
ate the whole answer, a safety block). @finish_reason@ is the wire's own token ("MAX_TOKENS",
"SAFETY", …).

It lives HERE and not in `ai` because it is not a fact about model steps: it is a fact about what this
API reports and how. It reaches an app as the `detail` of an `ai.provider_error`, which is the arm the
neutral error surface keeps for exactly this — so an app that wants to dispatch on the finish reason
matches this datum out of the detail, and one that does not still sees a message and a transience
verdict.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

declarations.documentation:
Serve `ai.infer_step` over OpenAI for the extent of the continuation:
`use openai.provider(source = credentials.env(key = "OPENAI_API_KEY"))`.
A step's provider failure (`ai.step_error`) is handed back as an `ai.inference_failed` OUTCOME, never
thrown — but a TRANSIENT one (a 429 rate limit, a 5xx, a dropped connection) is first retried with
exponential backoff (up to @retry_attempts@ attempts from @retry_base_milliseconds@); only a fatal error
or an exhausted budget surfaces, as a value the loop handles at its own perform site rather than a throw.
Prompt caching is per-PROVIDER machinery and nothing here asks for it: OpenAI caches a repeated prefix
AUTOMATICALLY, off the bytes it already receives. (Anthropic is the one that needs explicit
`cache_control` breakpoints, which `anthropic.provider` places for you.)
declarations.name: provider

parameters.documentation:
The Chat Completions model id. Defaults to `gpt-4o-mini`: it is the general-purpose workhorse of the
series this module is written against, it is reachable by every key that can reach the endpoint at all,
and a DEFAULT is what runs when nobody chose — so the cheapest capable model is the honest one to put
there, exactly as `gemini.provider` defaults to a flash model. A program with an opinion passes it.

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:

on success. A provider's per-attempt helper catches a `step_error` into `attempt_err` so the loop can
classify it (`is_transient`) and either back off and retry or propagate.

context the step consumed (every provider re-reads the full history each step), so the FRESHEST
step's figure IS the session's current context occupancy — figures across steps do not add.

escalation instead.)

the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its

anyOf.description:
provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
missing_secret: No secret env entry is set under @key@. Thrown by `get_secret` — catch it to fall back in-program
(`use handler { request throw(error: env.missing_secret) -> never { ... } }`).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

key.description: The key that had no secret entry.

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
server_error: The OAuth token could not be resolved for a TRANSIENT reason — a network error, or the token endpoint
failing (5xx) while refreshing. Thrown by `token`. Catch it to control retry — a retried call re-resolves.
(A credential that needs a human to (re)authorize is never a throw: the run pauses on an authorization
escalation instead.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

reply to JSON conforming to @schema@. The name map is empty — a replayed call turn in @history@
rides under its real name via the fallback, fine for the rare structured step over a tool
transcript. The reply content parses back to the decoded object; a non-JSON reply throws
`json.parse_error` (∈ `ai.step_error`).

provider_error: A step failure only the PROVIDER can name — the arm that keeps `step_error` from being a list of
transport shapes and lets a provider carry its own failure as a value. @source@ says who produced it
(a provider module's name, or a middleware's), @message@ is the one human-readable line an app can
show, @transient@ is the PROVIDER's own verdict on whether trying again could help (`is_transient`
reads it rather than guessing about a failure it has never seen), and @detail@ carries the provider's
own typed datum — so an app that knows the provider can `match` it out, and one that does not still
has a message and a verdict.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

detail.description: The producer's own typed datum, for an app that wants to match on it.

message.description: One human-readable line.

source.description: Who produced this failure — the provider module or middleware that built it.

transient.description: The producer's own verdict: could a retry help?

anyOf.description:
missing_secret: No secret env entry is set under @key@. Thrown by `get_secret` — catch it to fall back in-program
(`use handler { request throw(error: env.missing_secret) -> never { ... } }`).

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

key.description: The key that had no secret entry.

anyOf.description:
api_error: An authenticated API call failed for anything OTHER than the credential: a non-2xx @status@ that is not
401/403 — a malformed request, a resource that is not there, a rate limit, a server error. Nothing about
the caller's identity is in question, so backing off and replaying the call AS IT STANDS is the whole
recovery for the transient half, and the other half (a 400 the service is simply refusing) will keep
failing until the ARGUMENT changes.

WHICH half a given failure is, is read off @status@ and nowhere else: 408 / 429 / 5xx are the transient
ones a retry policy should back off and repeat, every other status is a refusal that will repeat forever.
That is the whole reason the status RIDES on the error instead of being folded into a sentence — a retry
policy downstream reads a number, never a message.

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words; @message@ carries the server's own body
verbatim, because it is the diagnosis and a model handed this error reads it and adjusts.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "tavily.search").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
auth_error: An authenticated API call was rejected over WHO IS CALLING: the endpoint answered @status@ — 401 or
403 — so the CREDENTIAL is what failed: revoked, expired past what its holder believed, or scoped too
narrowly for this call. Retrying with the SAME credential cannot succeed; the recovery is a fresh
RESOLUTION of it, which is why the ordinary composition is a `replay` converter that signals
`replay.interrupted`: the re-run resolves the credential again, and one the runtime cannot refresh parks
the run on a `prelude.oauth.authorize` escalation — a human's re-authorization prompt — rather than
failing. That is the whole line this variant draws: an `auth_error` may need a HUMAN before any retry can
work, an `api_error` never does.

(403 is read as auth even though some APIs also spend it on quota exhaustion. The access-rejection reading
is the one worth composing a re-resolution around, and a quota 403 that is replayed simply fails again.)

@context@ says WHICH call failed in the caller's own words, and @message@ carries the server's own body —
the two halves a human needs, kept apart so a renderer can show either without splitting a string.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

context.description: Which call failed, in the caller's own words — for a human reading the error (e.g. "gmail.send").

message.description: The response body, or the reason the caller has instead.

anyOf.description:
fetch_error: An HTTP request never completed: DNS failure, refused connection, timeout, or a mid-flight runtime
restart. Thrown by `fetch`. (A response that did arrive is never an error — branch on its `status`.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description: parse_error: A JSON document failed to parse: the text is not JSON. Thrown by `parse` / `parse_as`.

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

anyOf.description:
server_error: The OAuth token could not be resolved for a TRANSIENT reason — a network error, or the token endpoint
failing (5xx) while refreshing. Thrown by `token`. Catch it to control retry — a retried call re-resolves.
(A credential that needs a human to (re)authorize is never a throw: the run pauses on an authorization
escalation instead.)

$katari_constructor.description: The tag that selects this variant. Write this exact string.

declarations.documentation:
THE correlation handle of one tool call: a single OPAQUE token, minted by the provider that parsed
the model's pick and replayed verbatim on the call turn AND on the result that answers it. WHAT it
holds is the provider's own business — an id its wire keys a result by, or a token its wire demands
echoed back on the call — and nothing above the provider ever reads it. It exists so a result and its
call correlate by carrying the SAME value, which is one channel rather than a choice between two
mutually exclusive keys.
declarations.name: call_ref

declaration or replaying a call turn), @wire_to_real@ by the wire name (used to reverse the model's
pick); both are total over one step's tools — see @build_name_map@.
declarations.name: name_map

these APIs share (the dot of a qualified name, above all) folds to `_`, then the result is capped at
their 64-character limit.

declarations.documentation:
Choose a free wire name for @real@ given the wire names already @taken@: its sanitized form, or —
when sanitizing collapsed two distinct qualified names onto one token, or truncation shared a prefix —
the first free ordinal-suffixed form. The suffix is decided by @taken@'s size (processing order), so
the choice is deterministic.

declarations.documentation:
Build the deterministic wire-name @name_map@ for one step's tools. Walking @tool_metas@ in order,
each tool's qualified name is assigned a free wire name against the names already placed, so the same
tool list always yields the same map — which is why the map needs no durable state (see the module
note). A provider whose wire vocabulary admits the qualified name never imports this module at all.
declarations.name: build_name_map
